title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An AI agent was used to conduct post-exploitation activity following an initial compromise through a known vulnerability in marimo notebooks. The agent adapted its attacks in real time to an unknown target environment, composing commands dynamically rather than executing pre-written scripts, and successfully moved from initial access through credential theft to database exfiltration in under one hour. The attack involved harvesting cloud credentials, retrieving an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager, and using distributed SSH sessions to steal an internal PostgreSQL database within two minutes.

This represents a failure in runtime detection and containment. The system had no observable check on what an authenticated attacker with access to cloud credentials and SSH keys could do once inside, or on the lateral movement patterns that would distinguish an AI agent's behavior from legitimate administration. It would have required either detection of the reconnaissance queries and command composition pattern, or restrictions on the scope of what credentials could access once harvested.

It is not established whether marimo instances were exposed without authentication, whether the initial compromise required any special access, or whether the organization had any visibility into the cloud credential stores or SSH key management before the exfiltration occurred.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
On May 10, 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team detected an intrusion where an AI agent orchestrated a sophisticated attack. The attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebooks to gain initial access, then harvested cloud credentials and used them to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager. The attacker then leveraged Cloudflare Workers to distribute eight parallel SSH sessions across multiple IP addresses, successfully exfiltrating an internal PostgreSQL database schema and contents within two minutes. The entire attack chain from initial compromise to database theft completed in under one hour.

The attack demonstrates a critical shift in how sophisticated intrusions operate. Rather than executing pre-written scripts, the LLM agent composed commands in real time, adapting to the unknown target environment. Key evidence includes improvised database dumps targeting tables the attacker had no prior knowledge of, planning comments embedded in the command stream, commands formatted for machine parsing rather than human interaction, and the agent consuming its own output to drive subsequent actions. Organizations should immediately patch marimo to version 0.23.0 or later, audit and rotate credentials on all marimo instances, and deploy runtime threat detection to identify agent-driven lateral movement.
